question: According to Census of India 2011, what was the total population of India (approx)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 121 Crore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, the total population of India was about 121 crore (1,210 million / 1.21 billion) — precisely 1,210,854,977. (भारत की जनसंख्या 2011 — लगभग 121 करोड़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India and the 7th after Independence. Its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future".

• Density of population: 382 persons per sq. km. Sex ratio: 943 females per 1000 males. Literacy rate: 74.04%.

• Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim. Most populous UT — Delhi.

• Highest literacy — Kerala (93.91%); lowest — Bihar (61.8%). Highest sex ratio — Kerala (1084); lowest — Haryana (879).

NOTE

• The Census in India is conducted every 10 years under the Census Act, 1948, by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, Ministry of Home Affairs.

• The first census in India was held in 1872 under Lord Mayo; the first complete, synchronous census was in 1881 under Lord Ripon.

question: Chhau is a major dance tradition of India. In which of the following Indian states is the dance form NOT prevalent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhau is a semi-classical, martial folk dance tradition practised in three eastern states — Odisha, West Bengal and Jharkhand. It is NOT prevalent in Madhya Pradesh. (छऊ नृत्य — ओडिशा, पश्चिम बंगाल, झारखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The three recognised styles of Chhau are:

◦ Seraikela Chhau — Jharkhand (dancers wear masks).

◦ Purulia Chhau — West Bengal (large, elaborate masks).

◦ Mayurbhanj Chhau — Odisha (performed without masks).

• Chhau blends martial arts (Pharikhanda), acrobatics and athletics with themes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas.

• It was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

NOTE

• Folk dances of Madhya Pradesh include Gaur, Matki, Grida, Phulpati, Karma and Jawara — not Chhau.

• India's eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: In November 2022, which state became the first North-East state to approve Mental Health and Social Care Policy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2022, Meghalaya became the first North-Eastern state (and one of the first in India) to approve a dedicated "Mental Health and Social Care Policy". (मेघालय — मानसिक स्वास्थ्य नीति)

• The policy aims to make mental-health care accessible, affordable and stigma-free, integrating counselling and social care into primary health services.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Meghalaya ("the abode of clouds") became a full state on 21 January 1972; capital — Shillong. Major tribes: Khasi, Jaintia and Garo.

• At the national level, mental health is governed by the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, which decriminalised attempted suicide and guaranteed the right to access mental healthcare.

• The National Tele Mental Health Programme (Tele-MANAS) was launched in October 2022.

NOTE

• The National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) has been running since 1982; the District Mental Health Programme (DMHP) was added in 1996.

• World Mental Health Day is observed on 10 October every year.

question: In which state is Vishakhapatnam Port located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Visakhapatnam Port is located in the state of Andhra Pradesh, on the east coast of India along the Bay of Bengal. (विशाखापत्तनम बंदरगाह — आंध्र प्रदेश)

• It is one of India's major ports and is famous as the deepest landlocked port in the country, handling large volumes of iron ore, coal and petroleum.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Visakhapatnam is also the headquarters of the Eastern Naval Command of the Indian Navy and hosts Hindustan Shipyard.

• Major ports on the east coast: Kolkata (Syama Prasad Mookerjee), Paradip (Odisha), Visakhapatnam (AP), Chennai, Kamarajar/Ennore (TN), V. O. Chidambaranar/Tuticorin (TN).

• Major ports on the west coast: Kandla (Deendayal, Gujarat), Mumbai, Jawaharlal Nehru (Nhava Sheva), Mormugao (Goa), New Mangalore (Karnataka), Cochin (Kerala).

NOTE

• India has 13 major ports (12 government-administered plus Port Blair). Major ports come under the Union Government (Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways); minor ports are under state governments.

question: Who among the following is the Indian classical dancer who masters both Bharatanatyam and Odissi dancing style?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonal Mansingh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sonal Mansingh is the celebrated Indian classical dancer who has mastered both Bharatanatyam and Odissi. (सोनल मानसिंह — भरतनाट्यम एवं ओडिसी)

• She was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2003) — becoming the first woman dancer to receive it — and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. She was later nominated to the Rajya Sabha (2018).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shovana Narayan — a renowned exponent of Kathak (and a former Indian Audit and Accounts Service officer).

• Guru Bipin Singh — the great guru of Manipuri dance.

• Padma Subrahmanyam — a leading exponent of Bharatanatyam and the creator of "Bharata Nrityam".

• Sonal Mansingh founded the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CICD), New Delhi, in 1977.

NOTE

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha, characterised by the tribhanga posture and sculpturesque poses derived from temple carvings; Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra.

question: Which bacteria was discovered by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren that colonises the human stomach and causes chronic superficial gastritis ulcers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helicobacter pylori.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is the spiral-shaped bacterium discovered by the Australian scientists Barry Marshall and Robin Warren. It colonises the human stomach lining and causes chronic superficial gastritis, peptic ulcers and, in some cases, stomach cancer. (हेलिकोबैक्टर पाइलोरी)

• For this discovery the two were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2005.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Campylobacter jejuni — a common cause of food poisoning / bacterial diarrhoea.

• Neisseria gonorrhoeae — the bacterium that causes the sexually transmitted disease gonorrhoea.

• Entamoeba histolytica — not a bacterium at all but a protozoan parasite, which causes amoebic dysentery.

• H. pylori survives the stomach's acid by producing the enzyme urease, which neutralises acid around it.

NOTE

• Before this discovery, ulcers were blamed on stress and spicy food; today they are treated with antibiotics plus proton-pump inhibitors. Barry Marshall famously drank a culture of the bacteria himself to prove the link.

question: Which of the following states witnesses the first onset of the monsoon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kerala witnesses the first onset of the South-West Monsoon in India, normally around 1 June every year. The moisture-laden winds of the Arabian Sea branch strike the Western Ghats first and give Kerala its first heavy showers. (केरल — मानसून का प्रथम आगमन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The South-West Monsoon advances from Kerala northwards, covering the whole country by about 15 July, and begins to withdraw from north-west India around mid-September.

• The monsoon has two branches — the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch. Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Meghalaya) receive the highest rainfall in the world.

• Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh are reached last, in late June–early July, and receive comparatively less monsoon rain.

NOTE

• The India Meteorological Department (IMD), established in 1875 with headquarters at New Delhi, officially declares the onset of the monsoon over Kerala.

• The North-East (retreating) Monsoon brings winter rainfall mainly to Tamil Nadu and the Coromandel Coast in October–December.

question: What is a prominent trend in the microfinance sector in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Integration of mobile banking services.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A prominent, well-documented trend in India's microfinance sector is the integration of mobile banking and digital financial services. Microfinance institutions (MFIs) now use mobile apps, UPI, Aadhaar-enabled payments and e-KYC to disburse loans, collect repayments and reach remote borrowers cheaply. (माइक्रोफाइनेंस में मोबाइल बैंकिंग का एकीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options describe the opposite of current trends: the sector is moving towards faster, technology-driven approvals, greater (not decreased) reliance on digital technology, and a strong focus on women borrowers — women form the overwhelming majority of microfinance clients through Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups.

• Microfinance provides small-value loans, savings and insurance to low-income households that lack access to formal banking.

• NABARD launched the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme in 1992, the world's largest microfinance programme.

NOTE

• The Reserve Bank of India regulates NBFC-MFIs; its revised Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans (2022) defines a microfinance loan as a collateral-free loan to a household with annual income up to ₹3 lakh.

• Bandhan Bank began as a microfinance institution before becoming a universal bank; Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh (Grameen Bank) is called the "father of microfinance" and won the Nobel Peace Prize (2006).

question: Ustad Bismillah Khan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shehnai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916–2006) was the legendary Indian musician associated with the "Shehnai", a double-reed wind (aerophone) instrument traditionally played at weddings and temple ceremonies. He almost single-handedly raised the shehnai to the concert stage. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान — शहनाई)

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, India's highest civilian honour, and also the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He famously played the shehnai from the Red Fort on 15 August 1947, on India's first Independence Day, at the invitation of Pandit Nehru.

• Other instruments and their masters:

◦ Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, Ustad Ali Akbar Khan.

◦ Sitar — Pandit Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan.

◦ Sarangi — Pandit Ram Narayan.

NOTE

• Classification of Indian instruments: Tata Vadya (string — sitar, sarod, veena), Sushira Vadya (wind — shehnai, flute, nadaswaram), Avanaddha Vadya (percussion with membrane — tabla, mridangam), Ghana Vadya (solid/idiophone — manjira, jaltarang).

question: The famous coal mining region ‘Korba’ is located in which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Korba, one of India's most important coal mining regions, is located in the state of Chhattisgarh. It lies in the Hasdeo river valley and is famous for both its coalfields and its huge thermal power plants. (कोरबा — छत्तीसगढ़)

• Korba is often called the "Power Capital of India" because of the large NTPC and CSEB thermal power stations there.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's coal reserves lie mainly in the Gondwana rock formations of eastern and central India — Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh and Telangana.

• Other famous coalfields: Jharia, Bokaro, Giridih (Jharkhand); Raniganj (West Bengal); Talcher (Odisha); Singrauli (MP); Singareni (Telangana).

• Jharkhand and Odisha are the largest coal-producing states of India.

NOTE

• Types of coal in decreasing order of carbon content and quality: Anthracite (best) > Bituminous > Lignite > Peat (poorest). Most Indian coal is bituminous; lignite is found mainly at Neyveli (Tamil Nadu).

• Coal India Limited (CIL), established in 1975, is the world's largest coal-producing company.

question: What do you mean by balanced budget?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Expenditure equal to revenue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "balanced budget" is one in which the government's total estimated expenditure is exactly equal to its total estimated revenue/receipts for a financial year. (संतुलित बजट — व्यय = आय)

◦ Balanced budget: Total Expenditure = Total Revenue.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Surplus budget — revenue exceeds expenditure (Revenue > Expenditure). It is used to control inflation by withdrawing money from circulation.

• Deficit budget — expenditure exceeds revenue (Expenditure > Revenue). Recommended by J. M. Keynes during a depression, as it boosts demand and employment; India generally presents a deficit budget.

• Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − Total receipts (excluding borrowings). Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts. Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest payments.

NOTE

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the "Annual Financial Statement". Since 2017 it is presented on 1 February, and the Railway Budget was merged with it in the same year.

• The FRBM Act, 2003 (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management) sets targets for reducing fiscal and revenue deficits.

question: Rajgir Mahotsav is a beautiful representation of history, religion, art and culture. It is a three-day celebration in ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Rajgir Mahotsav" is a three-day cultural festival celebrated at Rajgir in the Nalanda district of Bihar. It showcases the region's history, religion, art and culture through folk dances, classical music, opera and handicrafts. (राजगीर महोत्सव — बिहार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rajgir (ancient Rajagriha) was the first capital of the Magadha empire under the Haryanka dynasty (Bimbisara and Ajatashatru) before the capital shifted to Pataliputra.

• The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajgir (Saptaparni caves) in 483 BCE under the patronage of Ajatashatru. Rajgir is also sacred to Jainism — Lord Mahavira spent many rainy seasons here.

• Rajgir is famous for its hot springs (Brahmakund), the Vishwa Shanti Stupa (Peace Pagoda), Griddhakuta hill and India's first Ropeway. Nearby lies the ancient Nalanda University (a UNESCO World Heritage Site).

NOTE

• Other festivals of Bihar: Chhath Puja, Sonepur Mela (Asia's largest cattle fair), Pitrapaksha Mela (Gaya), Bihula-Bishahari and Sama-Chakeva.

question: The famous novel ‘The God Of Small Things’ is written by ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The God of Small Things" (1997) is the celebrated debut novel of the Indian author Arundhati Roy. It won the Booker Prize in 1997, making her the first Indian woman to win the award. (अरुंधति रॉय)

• The novel is set in Ayemenem, Kerala, and tells the story of the fraternal twins Rahel and Estha, exploring caste, family and forbidden love.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Her second novel is "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness" (2017). Her non-fiction includes "The End of Imagination", "Walking with the Comrades" and "Listening to Grasshoppers".

• Shashi Tharoor — The Great Indian Novel, An Era of Darkness, Why I Am a Hindu.

• Ruskin Bond — The Room on the Roof, The Blue Umbrella, A Flight of Pigeons.

• Vikram Seth — A Suitable Boy, The Golden Gate, An Equal Music.

NOTE

• Indian-origin Booker Prize winners: V. S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981 – Midnight's Children), Arundhati Roy (1997), Kiran Desai (2006 – The Inheritance of Loss), Aravind Adiga (2008 – The White Tiger). Geetanjali Shree won the International Booker Prize (2022) for Tomb of Sand (Ret Samadhi).

question: The Men's Junior Hockey Asia Cup 2023, which was won by India, was held at _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Oman.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Men's Junior Hockey Asia Cup 2023 was held at Salalah, Oman, and was won by India, who defeated Pakistan 2–1 in the final. (जूनियर हॉकी एशिया कप 2023 — ओमान)

• This was India's fourth Junior Asia Cup title (after 2004, 2008 and 2015).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The tournament is organised by the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) and acts as a qualifier for the Junior Hockey World Cup.

• India's captain in the 2023 edition was Uttam Singh, who was also adjudged the Player of the Tournament.

• Hockey India is the governing body for hockey in India; the international federation is the FIH (Fédération Internationale de Hockey), founded in 1924.

NOTE

• India's men's hockey team has won 8 Olympic gold medals (1928–1980) and the 1975 World Cup. At the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, India won a bronze medal after 41 years.

• Major Dhyan Chand, the "Wizard of Hockey", is honoured with National Sports Day on 29 August, his birth anniversary.

question: In the context of the Revolt of 1857, Mangal Pandey belonged to which Bengal native Infantry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 34.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mangal Pandey was a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry, stationed at Barrackpore (near Kolkata). On 29 March 1857 he attacked his British officers, and he was hanged on 8 April 1857 — an act widely regarded as the spark of the Revolt of 1857. (मंगल पांडे — 34वीं बंगाल नेटिव इन्फैंट्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The immediate cause of the revolt was the introduction of the Enfield rifle, whose greased cartridges (rumoured to contain cow and pig fat) had to be bitten open, offending both Hindu and Muslim sepoys.

• The revolt formally broke out at Meerut on 10 May 1857, and the rebels marched to Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar as Emperor of India.

• Centres and leaders: Delhi – Bakht Khan; Kanpur – Nana Sahib & Tantia Tope; Lucknow – Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi – Rani Lakshmibai; Bihar (Jagdishpur) – Kunwar Singh; Bareilly – Khan Bahadur Khan; Faizabad – Maulvi Ahmadullah.

NOTE

• After the revolt, the Government of India Act, 1858 ended East India Company rule and transferred power to the British Crown; Lord Canning became the first Viceroy of India.

• V. D. Savarkar called the revolt "The First War of Indian Independence".

question: Which of the following countries did India beat in the final to win the 2021 SAFF Championship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nepal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won the 2021 SAFF Championship (held in Malé, Maldives, in October 2021) by beating Nepal 3–0 in the final. (सैफ चैंपियनशिप 2021 — भारत ने नेपाल को हराया)

• Sunil Chhetri scored twice and Suresh Singh Wangjam once in the final; Chhetri was the tournament's leading Indian scorer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This was India's 8th SAFF Championship title. India later won the 2023 SAFF Championship as well, beating Kuwait on penalties in Bengaluru — making it India's 9th title.

• The SAFF (South Asian Football Federation) Championship began in 1993 and involves India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Maldives and Bhutan.

• Sunil Chhetri is India's all-time leading goal-scorer and one of the highest international scorers among active players.

NOTE

• The All India Football Federation (AIFF) was founded in 1937; India's national football team is nicknamed the "Blue Tigers".

• India's best performance in the Asian Games football was gold in 1951 and 1962.

question: Vinesh Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to win how many medals at World Championships?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vinesh Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to win two medals at the World Wrestling Championships — a bronze in 2019 (Nur-Sultan, Kazakhstan) and another bronze in 2022 (Belgrade, Serbia). (विनेश फोगाट — विश्व चैंपियनशिप में दो पदक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Vinesh Phogat is also the first Indian woman wrestler to win gold at both the Asian Games (2018, Jakarta) and the Commonwealth Games (2014, 2018, 2022).

• She was awarded the Arjuna Award (2016) and the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna / Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (2020).

• She belongs to the famous Phogat wrestling family of Haryana; her cousins Geeta and Babita Phogat inspired the film Dangal.

NOTE

• Indian wrestlers who have won Olympic medals: K. D. Jadhav (1952 bronze), Sushil Kumar (2008 bronze, 2012 silver), Yogeshwar Dutt (2012 bronze), Sakshi Malik (2016 bronze), Ravi Dahiya (2020 silver), Bajrang Punia (2020 bronze).

• Sakshi Malik was the first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal (Rio 2016).

question: What is the purpose of the Cultural and Educational Rights?
option_2: To protect the language, culture, and religion of the minority communities
solution_text:
The correct answer is To protect the language, culture, and religion of the minority communities.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29 and 30) are intended to protect the language, script, culture and religion of minority communities and to enable them to preserve their distinct identity. (सांस्कृतिक एवं शैक्षिक अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 29-30)

◦ Article 29 — Protection of the interests of minorities: any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture has the right to conserve it; no citizen shall be denied admission to a State-aided institution on grounds of religion, race, caste or language.

◦ Article 30 — Right of all minorities (religious or linguistic) to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The six Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Constitution are:

◦ Right to Equality (Articles 14–18)

◦ Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22)

◦ Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24)

◦ Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28)

◦ Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29–30)

◦ Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32)

• "To prevent exploitation" is the purpose of Articles 23–24 (prohibition of human trafficking, forced labour and child labour), not of Articles 29–30.

NOTE

• The Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment (1978) and made a legal right under Article 300A.

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the "heart and soul of the Constitution".

question: In optics, which term refers to the opening of the diaphragm of a lens that spatially limits the propagation of light?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aperture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In optics, the "aperture" is the opening of the diaphragm of a lens through which light passes; it spatially limits the propagation of light and thus controls how much light reaches the image/sensor. (द्वारक / एपर्चर)

• The aperture size is expressed as an f-number (f/stop), e.g., f/2.8, f/8. A smaller f-number = a wider aperture = more light and a shallower depth of field.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Collimator — an optical device that narrows a beam of light so that the rays become parallel; used in spectrometers and telescopes.

• Apostilb — an old unit of luminance (brightness).

• Meniscus — a lens that is convex on one side and concave on the other (also the curved upper surface of a liquid in a tube).

NOTE

• In photography the "exposure triangle" is aperture + shutter speed + ISO.

• Other optics terms for SSC: focal length (distance from the lens to its focus), power of a lens = 1/focal length in metres (unit dioptre), magnification, and the lens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.

question: Lata Mangeshkar was awarded by the India's highest civilian honour ‘Bharat Ratna’ in the year _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2001.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar was conferred the "Bharat Ratna", India's highest civilian honour, in the year 2001. (लता मंगेशकर — भारत रत्न, 2001)

• She was only the second singer/musician to receive it, after M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Lata Mangeshkar (1929–2022), called the "Nightingale of India" (स्वर कोकिला), recorded songs in over 36 languages. Her other honours include the Padma Bhushan (1969), Padma Vibhushan (1999) and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1989).

• Her patriotic song "Aye Mere Watan Ke Logon" (1963), written by Pradeep, moved Pandit Nehru to tears.

• Interestingly, Ustad Bismillah Khan also received the Bharat Ratna in 2001, along with Lata Mangeshkar.

NOTE

• The Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954. The first recipients were Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, C. Rajagopalachari and Sir C. V. Raman.

• The youngest recipient is Sachin Tendulkar (2014); the first posthumous award went to Lal Bahadur Shastri (1966); the first woman recipient was Indira Gandhi (1971).

question: Nirmala Panikar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award-2019 (given in February 2023) for her contribution to _________ dance form.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nirmala Panikar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award-2019 (presented in February 2023) for her outstanding contribution to the "Mohiniyattam" dance form. (निर्मला पणिक्कर — मोहिनीअट्टम)

• She is a noted scholar-performer who has researched and revived traditional Mohiniyattam repertoire, and co-founded the Natanakaisiki dance school in Kerala.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mohiniyattam is the classical dance of Kerala, performed solo by women. Its name comes from "Mohini", the enchantress avatar of Lord Vishnu. It is marked by gentle, swaying (lasya) movements, off-white/gold kasavu costume, and songs in Manipravalam.

• Notable exponents: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma (called the "mother of Mohiniyattam"), Sunanda Nair, Bharati Shivaji, Kanak Rele.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, is India's national academy for music, dance and drama; its highest honour is the Akademi Ratna (Fellowship).

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Bharatanatyam – Tamil Nadu; Kathak – Uttar Pradesh; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam – Kerala; Kuchipudi – Andhra Pradesh; Odissi – Odisha; Manipuri – Manipur; Sattriya – Assam.

question: In which city is the Rajghat memorial situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Raj Ghat" memorial is situated in Delhi, on the western bank of the river Yamuna. It marks the cremation site of Mahatma Gandhi, who was assassinated on 30 January 1948. (राजघाट — दिल्ली)

• The memorial is a simple black marble platform bearing Gandhiji's last words "Hey Ram", with an eternal flame burning at one end.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other memorials ("Ghats") along the Yamuna in Delhi:

◦ Shanti Van — Jawaharlal Nehru

◦ Shakti Sthal — Indira Gandhi

◦ Vir Bhumi — Rajiv Gandhi

◦ Vijay Ghat — Lal Bahadur Shastri

◦ Kisan Ghat — Chaudhary Charan Singh

◦ Samta Sthal — Jagjivan Ram

• Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) and Sevagram Ashram (Wardha, Maharashtra) were Gandhiji's principal ashrams.

NOTE

• Mahatma Gandhi's birthday, 2 October, is observed as Gandhi Jayanti in India and as the International Day of Non-Violence by the United Nations.

• Gandhiji is called the "Father of the Nation"; the title "Mahatma" was given by Rabindranath Tagore.

question: In the 1939 Tripuri Congress Presidential Election, Pattabhi Sitaramayya was defeated by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhas Chandra Bose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the 1939 Tripuri session of the Indian National Congress, Subhas Chandra Bose defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya, the candidate backed by Mahatma Gandhi, in the presidential election by 1580 votes to 1377. (त्रिपुरी अधिवेशन 1939 — सुभाष चंद्र बोस की जीत)

• Gandhiji described the defeat as "my own defeat". Facing non-cooperation from the Congress Working Committee, Bose resigned the presidency in April 1939 and Rajendra Prasad took over.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• After resigning, Bose formed the "Forward Bloc" in 1939 within the Congress.

• Bose had earlier been elected Congress President at the Haripura session (1938).

• He later escaped from India, reached Germany and then South-East Asia, and reorganised the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) in 1943, giving the slogans "Give me blood and I will give you freedom", "Jai Hind" and "Chalo Delhi".

NOTE

• Important Congress sessions: 1885 Bombay (W. C. Bonnerjee – first session), 1907 Surat (split), 1916 Lucknow (Congress–League Pact), 1920 Nagpur (Non-Cooperation), 1929 Lahore (Purna Swaraj – Nehru), 1931 Karachi (Fundamental Rights), 1938 Haripura and 1939 Tripuri (Bose).

question: Whose autobiography is titled ‘Waiting for a Visa’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Waiting for a Visa" is the short autobiographical work of Dr. B. R. (Bhimrao) Ambedkar, written around 1935–36. In it he recounts, through personal incidents, the humiliation of untouchability he faced in India and abroad. (वेटिंग फॉर अ वीज़ा — डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर)

• The book is prescribed as a textbook in Columbia University, where Ambedkar himself had studied.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other important works of Dr. Ambedkar: "Annihilation of Caste", "The Problem of the Rupee", "Who Were the Shudras?", "The Buddha and His Dhamma", "Thoughts on Pakistan", "States and Minorities".

• He was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and India's first Law Minister. He is called the "Father of the Indian Constitution" and was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1990.

• He founded the newspapers Mooknayak (1920) and Bahishkrit Bharat, and signed the Poona Pact (1932) with Gandhiji.

NOTE

• Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia — socialist leader, author of Wheel of History. Dr. Rajendra Prasad — India's first President, author of Atmakatha and India Divided. Dr. Kamal Ranadive — a distinguished Indian cell biologist and cancer researcher.

question: In which year was the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2019.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act" was passed by Parliament in 2019 (assented to on 9 August 2019, effective from 31 October 2019). It bifurcated the state of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories — Jammu & Kashmir (with a legislature) and Ladakh (without a legislature). (जम्मू-कश्मीर पुनर्गठन अधिनियम, 2019)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Alongside it, on 5 August 2019, the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 was abrogated by a Presidential Order, and Article 35A ceased to operate.

• With this, the number of States became 28 and Union Territories became 9 (later 8 after the merger of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu in January 2020).

• 31 October is also observed as National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas), the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

NOTE

• Article 3 of the Constitution empowers Parliament to form new states and alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing states.

• Recent state formations: Telangana (2014, 29th state), Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand (2000).
